segments: 448 Chronography of Bar Hebraeus.
they snatched him.
And she began to weep,
and to scratch her face,
and to cry out wailing,
"Sire!
Sire!"
because she was deeply consumed with love for him.
But those captors did not turn back to her,
nor did they listen to her voice,
but they bound him,
and brought him from Tell Hamdun,
where they had seized him,
to the city of Sis,
and he was kept there in prison for about two years.
Now the Prince, his father,
even though he was a powerful man,
did not want to distress the Armenians,
lest in anger they should destroy his son.
Rather, he only kept sending envoys and entreating that they preserve him,
and he did not seek the kingdom from them.
And when he grew weary of sending envoys,
he came in person to Tell Hamdun,
and sent word to them to give him his son.
They, however, were persuaded {OCR? agreed},
and took him and went to the fortress called Amuda.
And they sent {OCR?} to the Prince,
that he should send to take his son.
And when he wished to take him,
it was said to him:
"Even if you take your son, he will not live,
because they have given him poison to drink,
and he cannot live more than ten days."
Which indeed happened.
For when the Prince departed and went away, thundering and threatening,
after a few days that Philip died,
and no one knew where they buried him.
Now when the Queen heard that he was dead,
she lost all hope of him,
and she left and went to the fortress of Seleucia on the seashore,
and took refuge with the Frères {Hospitallers}, the lords of the fortress,
and they protected her with honor.
And her mother came to her again from Cyprus—
this was a Frankish woman, the daughter of the King of Cyprus.
And when they gave her daughter to Philip,
they wished also to give her in marriage to Sire Geoffrey, the lord of the rock of Sarvand,
who was the son of Baron Smbat, the brother (son?) of Baron Constantine the Bailli.
And when she was not willing,
they drove her out of her country and she went to Cyprus.
And at this time she returned to her daughter,
and both of them remained in Seleucia until that Bailli brought them down by force.
Concerning the expedition of the Tatars against Sama{rquand?}: In this same year,
which is the year six hundred and eighteen (of the Arabs?),
after the Tatars had taken the city of Bukhara,
they came and encamped against the city of Samarkand.
